note.question: How can leverage and adverse selection generate recurring credit booms, freezes, and even chaotic asset-quality dynamics, and what policy removes those inefficient cycles?
note.overview: Price-taking entrepreneurs optimize borrowing or lending under a leverage constraint while unproductive rent-seekers supply observationally identical lemon assets. Their individually optimal choices aggregate into an adverse-selection credit-market equilibrium whose dynamic state can cycle; a constrained planner alters prices or taxes while respecting decentralized incentives.

components.label: Dynamic adverse-selection credit-market equilibrium
components.explanation: The model's equilibrium concept is Dynamic adverse-selection credit-market equilibrium. Section 2.1.3 defines equilibrium as a rental price and average asset quality together with optimal participation cutoffs satisfying capital-market clearing and the quality-consistency condition. Lemma 2 solves p and rho as functions of chi; Proposition 1 derives chi_{t+1}=Gamma(chi_t), and Lemma 5 characterizes instability and endogenous cycles.

components.label: Model sequence and system structure
components.explanation: In every period, agents enter with productive or lemon capital. Taking the rental price and pooled asset quality as given, entrepreneurs choose borrowing or lending and rent-seekers lend lemons. The credit market clears, production and saving occur, and the relative lemon stock becomes the next period's state. Low-productivity entrepreneurs lend productive capital, high-productivity entrepreneurs borrow, and intermediate types may abstain.
